findings.evidence: docs/spec/v1.md:94 requires idempotency keys for F03-F41 mutations, expected revisions for resource updates, and 409 for parameter collisions/stale revisions. backend-design.md:29-34 defines file commit/delete, trusted event publishing, custom routes and SDK contracts without any acceptance criterion for these inherited mutation semantics.
findings.refutation: The opening sentence incorporates existing V1 requirements, and file reservations may provide an upload identity. However, neither specifies retry/collision/revision behavior for the new mutating application contracts or a named test proving it; an upload ID alone does not prevent duplicate commits/events or stale metadata writes. The local-first scope does not waive the explicitly universal mutation contract.
findings.suggestion: Define the applicable idempotency, collision and expected-revision contract for application mutations and typed SDK calls, with named retry/concurrent/stale-write tests; explicitly resolve any native Better Auth endpoint exception.

findings.evidence: backend-design.md:8 leaves OAuth as opt-in configuration, while AC-54 at line 27 only names signup/signin/session/signout. tests/STRATEGY.md:28 requires a per-cell OAuth fixture in T14, including issuer/audience/origin/cookie isolation. docs/spec/v1.md:48 includes configured optional OAuth in F16.
findings.refutation: OAuth provider enrollment is properly excluded from this local tranche, and optional integrations need not be enabled by default. A disposable local provider fixture needs no real account enrollment, however, and is the acceptance evidence specifically requested by T14. Email/password success cannot demonstrate callback/state/provider identity scoping.
findings.suggestion: Add a local configured OAuth fixture acceptance case covering successful callback/session creation and wrong state/origin/provider/cell rejection; keep real provider enrollment unqualified.

findings.evidence: backend-design.md:30 limits AC-57 recovery evidence to manifests preserving metadata and identifying missing/incomplete files, and line 35 requires restart journeys. tests/STRATEGY.md:44 requires backup/restore of file/auth/config recovery sets and database-versus-file timestamp-gap display (T30); docs/spec/v1.md:88 requires validating restored identity/API flows in a separate recovery cell.
findings.refutation: Off-host recovery and automatic restore activation are correctly outside this tranche, and manifests are useful prerequisites. Actual local backup/restore into an isolated held destination can be verified without either remote qualification or activation. A restart of the source store/files cannot prove restored identity, committed object bytes, configuration binding or timestamp-gap handling.
findings.suggestion: Add a disposable local file/auth/config recovery round trip into a held destination, checking committed bytes/metadata, unfinished or missing objects, restored identity behavior and explicit timestamp-gap evidence; keep promotion blocked.

review_context.scope: Local E04 auth, files, SSE, custom TypeScript SDK and template design against F16-F19, T14-T17/T30/T34 and inherited V1 mutation contracts.
passed_observations: Per-cell independent application persistence and immutable server-owned configuration separate application users from owner identity and authority.
Private file defaults, server-owned physical names, finite concurrent quotas, resumable staging and committed-object preservation are explicit.
Authenticated durable SSE uses bounded cursors, explicit refetch gaps, lifecycle/revocation checks and finite stream resources.
SDK and control client have separate package ownership; the template requires explicit application authentication for route extensions.
Story order is acyclic and begins with identity/store authority; the E04 plan provides preservation/refetch/pinning failure checkpoints.
Every new acceptance criterion has a named T-AC identifier and remote qualification is explicitly excluded.
